summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes, chronic systolic heart failure, and bilateral below-knee amputations was readmitted due to hypotension after her PICC line dislodged during outpatient ertapenem therapy for recent Klebsiella sepsis. She received IV fluids, which resolved her hypotension. During admission, she was found to have C. difficile infection and candiduria with persistent pyuria, prompting treatment with oral vancomycin and fluconazole. A CT urogram showed tiny non-obstructing kidney stones but no anatomic abnormalities. Her insulin regimen was optimized to prevent hypoglycemia, lisinopril was held due to hypotension risk, and metoprolol was reduced. She was discharged home with nursing services, stable and afebrile, on a 10-day course of vancomycin and 14-day course of fluconazole, with follow-up arranged for her wounds and primary care.
